title: SECURITY DEFINER RPC `tenant_is_active` is an existence/status oracle for arbitrary tenant IDs
location: public.tenant_is_active(target_tenant_id uuid) — live DB (supabase-main), exposed via /rest/v1/rpc/tenant_is_active
description: The function is SECURITY DEFINER and EXECUTE-able by the `authenticated` role, but its body filters ONLY by the target_tenant_id parameter with no auth.uid()/caller-membership check (unlike its siblings auth_user_in_tenant and auth_user_can_access_conversation, which both constrain by auth.uid()). Any signed-in user can call the RPC with an arbitrary tenant UUID and learn whether that tenant exists and is active — a cross-tenant existence/status oracle. Practical exploitability is low because tenant IDs are unguessable UUIDs, but it violates least-privilege on the exposed API.
evidence: STABLE SECURITY DEFINER; body: SELECT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.tenants WHERE id = target_tenant_id AND status = 'active') — no auth.uid() predicate.
okWhen: The function is only ever intended to be called BY RLS policies (as definer), not directly by clients — in which case EXECUTE should be revoked from `authenticated` while policies keep using it.
notOkWhen: Signed-in users can call /rest/v1/rpc/tenant_is_active directly with a guessed/known tenant UUID (current state).
remediation: REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.tenant_is_active(uuid) FROM authenticated (RLS policies invoking it as definer are unaffected), or switch to SECURITY INVOKER, or add an auth.uid() membership check.
source: M1 connected (live DB DETECT-DEEPER, pg_get_functiondef + advisor 0029)

title: SECURITY DEFINER functions `auth_user_in_tenant` / `auth_user_can_access_conversation` verified caller-scoped (NOT findings)
description: Both advisor-flagged (0029) as authenticated-executable SECURITY DEFINER. Reading the bodies clears them: each constrains results by auth.uid() (the caller's own active user row within target_tenant_id), so a caller can only probe their OWN membership/conversation access — no cross-tenant data is returned. Recorded as verified-safe so the advisor WARN is adjudicated, not left ambiguous.
evidence: auth_user_in_tenant: WHERE auth_user_id = auth.uid() AND tenant_id = target_tenant_id AND status='active'. auth_user_can_access_conversation: constrains c.user_id to the auth.uid() user, or tenant_owner/agent of the same tenant.

title: Vestigial client SELECT grant on RLS-locked reference tables `pricing_seat_ladder` and `tier_definitions`
description: Both tables have RLS ENABLED with NO policy (deny-all to anon/authenticated) yet still grant SELECT to anon and authenticated. Because RLS-enabled-no-policy denies regardless of the grant, the SELECT grant is vestigial: the intended service-role-only reads work (service_role has BYPASSRLS), but any client SELECT via PostgREST silently returns empty. This is a hygiene/clarity issue, NOT a data leak (no cross-tenant rows are exposed). Both tables are documented as global service-role-only reference data (see table comments / PLATFORM_READABLE_TABLES).
evidence: role_table_grants: pricing_seat_ladder → anon SELECT, authenticated SELECT; tier_definitions → anon SELECT, authenticated SELECT. Both tables rls_enabled=true, 0 policies.
okWhen: The grant is intentional future-proofing and no client feature relies on reading these via the anon/authenticated key.
notOkWhen: A client feature is expected to read these tables via PostgREST — it will silently receive an empty result (broken feature), or the vestigial grant is simply removed for least-privilege.
remediation: REVOKE SELECT ON public.pricing_seat_ladder, public.tier_definitions FROM anon, authenticated (they are service-role-only), or add an explicit read policy if client reads are actually intended.
source: M1 connected (live DB DETECT-DEEPER, role_table_grants + advisor 0008)

title: 10 of 12 RLS-enabled-no-policy tables verified deny-all by design (incl. personal_access_tokens) — noted, not findings
location: public.{apify_spend_ledger, cruisemapper_url_inventory, destination_images, destination_images_cache, personal_access_tokens, pricing_cache, reconciliation_review_queue, stripe_price_map, supervisor_review_queue, vendor_health}
description: Advisor 0008 flagged 12 tables as RLS-enabled-no-policy. Checking role_table_grants: these 10 grant anon/authenticated only TRIGGER/TRUNCATE/REFERENCES (Supabase's default grants, none reachable via the PostgREST data API) — no SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE. RLS-enabled-no-policy is therefore deny-all to anon/authenticated by design, matching fp-rules ('RLS-enabled-no-policy on a service-role-only table is safe by design'). Notably personal_access_tokens (sensitive) is correctly locked.
evidence: No SELECT/DML grant to anon or authenticated on any of the 10; service_role (BYPASSRLS) reads them server-side.
okWhen: Always — deny-all by design; server-side service-role code is the only reader.
notOkWhen: N/A (verified). Contrast: RLS OFF with no policy would be exposed — not the case here (all 12 have RLS enabled).

title: Supabase Auth: leaked-password protection (HaveIBeenPwned) disabled
location: Supabase Auth config (project mfaknjyqiwcjojukcnea) — advisor auth_leaked_password_protection
description: Supabase Auth's compromised-password check against HaveIBeenPwned is disabled. If email/password sign-up is enabled, users can register/keep passwords known to be in breach corpora. A one-toggle hardening improvement.
evidence: Security advisor: auth_leaked_password_protection — 'Leaked password protection is currently disabled.'
okWhen: The project is OAuth/SSO-only (no email+password auth) — then this is N/A.
notOkWhen: Email/password auth is enabled for any tenant (verify in Auth providers).
remediation: Enable leaked-password protection in Supabase Auth settings; consider enabling minimum password strength.
